parts.text: Some students are investigating how the surface area of water exposed to the air affects the rate at which the water cools. They are using the apparatus shown in Fig. 1.1. Beaker B is bigger than beaker A . Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The students pour 75 cm 3 of hot water into beaker A and 75 cm 3 of hot water into beaker B . They immediately start a stopclock.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record, in the first row of Table 1.1, the initial temperatures θ of the water in beaker A and in beaker B , as shown in Fig. 1.1. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The students record the temperatures θ of the water every 30 s. Their readings are shown in Table 1.1. Complete the headings and the time t column in Table 1.1. [2] Table 1.1 beaker A beaker B t / θ / θ / 0 80.0 76.0 78.0 73.5 76.5 71.0 75.0 68.5 73.5 66.5 72.5 65.0

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text:
units all correct (symbols or words)
t values all present (30, 60, 90, 120, 150 and 180)

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
any 2 appropriate precautions:
e.g.
viewing perp. to thermometer scale (to avoid parallax)
stir before reading
keep thermometer at same level / not touching beaker walls
wait until reading stops rising at the start

ms.label: 1(c)(i)
ms.text:

15.0 and 9.5 °C, or 5.5 °C more)
statement that B cools more quickly / its temperature drops faster / its temperature falls more in the

ms.text:

less transfer of thermal energy / heat by sides
appropriate effect on values of θ:
e.g. all higher
